prompt: Our ticketing system will read the answers of the agent in helpdesk-triage/ and file them automatically, so a reply in prose is useless to it. Make every answer a JSON object with a category (billing, technical or account), a priority (low, medium or high) and a summary of at most 200 characters.

checks.expr: data.get('type') == 'object' and set(get(data, 'properties.category.enum') or []) == {'billing', 'technical', 'account'} and set(get(data, 'properties.priority.enum') or []) == {'low', 'medium', 'high'} and get(data, 'properties.summary.type') == 'string' and isinstance(get(data, 'properties.summary.maxLength'), int) and get(data, 'properties.summary.maxLength') <= 200 and {'category', 'priority', 'summary'} <= set(data.get('required') or [])
checks.why: the answer's shape is declared in app/response_schema.json (a JSON Schema, root object), not asked for in the prompt
lint checks the response schema and the agent's wiring (`Response schema: ... OK`)
a run on the fake model ends with a structured_response that has the asked keys and values
the template's structured answers are used as they are: no output tool of your own, no edit to app_utils

reference: Write app/response_schema.json: `{"type": "object", "properties": {"category": {"type": "string", "enum": ["billing", "technical", "account"]}, "priority": {"type": "string", "enum": ["low", "medium", "high"]}, "summary": {"type": "string", "maxLength": 200}}, "required": ["category", "priority", "summary"], "additionalProperties": false}`. A new project's agent.py already passes `response_format(model, tools)` and has `StructuredAnswer()` last, so nothing else changes; `graph-agents-cli lint` prints `Response schema: app/response_schema.json OK`. The run delivers the object as `structured_response` (and as the only `message.delta`). Never ask for JSON in the system prompt, parse it from the reply, or add an output tool.
